name: Unprovable sandbox → park toward the human (fail closed)
description:
The fail-closed park (design SB5). When provision_sandbox cannot prove the sandbox ready — docker absent, an undeclared/unbuildable image, a repo that does not build cold, a missing secret, or a claim only an operator-ci/lab tier can prove — it records the reason on the run as sandbox.blocked and stamps NO readiness. This rule reads that block and PARKS the run toward the human: it records run.awaiting_human (the reason) on the run entity and posts the question to the channel-agnostic user-response bus. No Go reconciler, backstop ticker, or app-side state machine advances a run whose sandbox could not be proven (G2/B3/B7) — the readiness gate (dev-from-task/02 requires sandbox.ready eq true) already holds the dev loop, and this makes the hold an honest, surfaced park rather than a silent stall. This is the semspec disease inverted: a nil/absent/unprovable sandbox NEVER passes verify or records a hollow attempt — it parks.

WRITER: run.awaiting_human's writer is the park-rule subsystem (G5) — the same logical writer as run-lifecycle/03-park-awaiting-human. Both rules mean the identical thing (this run awaits a human, here is why) and upsert the one park marker the whole system reads (the D15 park-exclusion forward-contract keys on run.awaiting_human); they differ only in TRIGGER (a coordinator ask_human decision vs an unprovable sandbox). Rule add_triple carries no Source, so there is no runtime writer drift — the vocab keeps the single run.awaiting_human entry and this is a second realization of that one park writer, not a second predicate.

SUBJECT: unlike run-lifecycle/03 (which fires on a COORDINATOR loop and redirects the marker to agent.run.entity_id), this fires on the RUN entity itself — sandbox.blocked is stamped on the run by provision_sandbox — so the marker goes on $entity.id directly, no redirect. sandbox.blocked ne "" uniquely identifies a blocked run (the tool stamps it only on run entities).

FIRE-ONCE: the run.awaiting_human length_eq 0 guard makes this park once — the marker its own action stamps flips the trigger false, so it does not re-post to the user bus on every re-scan (the same self-limiting shape as run-lifecycle/03). A human resume path (group 5 forge-io) clears run.awaiting_human to un-park.
